name: Mnemite-SX
description: A titanium-nickel-vanadium alloy manufactured at the nano-grain level by Crucible Industries, Mnemite-SX can be programmed with up to twelve distinct geometric configurations and triggered to return to any stored form via thermal, electrical, or acoustic stimulus. The alloy's crystalline memory is encoded during a high-pressure quantum-annealing process that locks phase-transition temperatures to within 0.3°C tolerances. Unlike legacy shape-memory alloys, Mnemite-SX retains configuration fidelity after tens of thousands of cycles without fatigue degradation.
applications: Deployable medical implants that conform post-insertion
Reconfigurable chassis components for modular vehicles
Tactical gear clasps and restraints with remote-release
Architectural elements that adjust to seismic load
story_hooks: A runner discovers their black-market Mnemite-SX bone plate is still programmed with someone else's configuration — and it begins activating at random, suggesting the original owner may be sending a signal.

A Tier 3 fabricator has cracked how to re-encode Mnemite-SX using salvaged annealing rigs, undercutting Crucible Industries prices — and someone from the corponation's enforcement division wants that operation buried.

A collapsed building traps survivors behind a sealed door made of Mnemite-SX structural panels; someone with the right trigger frequency could open it — if they can figure out what form the panels are programmed to return to.
